title: Eventflow retention tiering and cost allocator for audit pipeline
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Audit event ingestion is growing faster than projections for some large tenants and internal subsystems. Current flat retention policies cause disproportionate cost in indexing and query hotspots. We need a policy-driven retention and partitioning system ("eventflow tiering") that assigns write affinity, enforces per-tenant cost quotas, and gracefully demotes older data to cold storage with searchable lightweight indexes.

Goal: Implement an "affinity-based partition allocator" + "cost allocator" that: 1) routes high-cardinality streams into optimized write partitions, 2) applies tiered TTLs and compaction schedules per tenant/stream class, 3) integrates with RBAC v2 signals so privileged admin events are retained differently, and 4) surfaces cost signals and alerts in Console.

Non-goals: Full replacement of existing shard controller in this cycle; we will provide a backward-compatible controller that coexists with current ingest topology and can be progressively enabled per region/cluster.
acceptance_criteria: Affinity allocator assigns new streams to partitions with tenant and topic metadata and persists allocation decisions in config store
Per-tenant monthly ingest quota is enforced; events over quota are sampled at configurable rates and tagged in the event envelope
Tiered retention policies (hot 7d, warm 30d, cold 365d) can be declared per-tenant/stream and executed by the lifecycle manager
Cold tiered blobs are queryable via a lightweight sparse index that preserves audit query semantics with <=5% miss rate for common queries
Admin/SSO/SAML critical events are flagged and excluded from aggressive downsampling unless explicitly scoped
Console shows token-level cost breakdown for audit ingestion and an estimator for cost impact of retention changes
Canary rollout in one region with clear rollback path and migration playbook
implementation_notes:
High-level design: 1) Ingest Agent: augment the event envelope with tenant_id, stream_class, rbac_label (derived from RBAC v2), and allocation_hint. 2) Affinity Allocator: service that computes partition affinity using tenant weight, recent write QPS, and topology capacity. Stores assignments in ZooKeeper/etcd as ephemeral + versioned configs. 3) Cost Allocator: sliding-window counters + smoothing that emits per-tenant quota state; exposes throttle/sampling decisions via response header and event flag. 4) Lifecycle Manager: executes TTL demotion schedule; moves segments to cold blobstore (S3 glacier-like) and writes sparse indices. 5) Query Adapter: when reading, the adapter consults sparse index and, if necessary, lazily fetches cold blobs. 6) Observability: add meters for partition size, demotion rate, cold-read latency, and cost-estimate per tenant.

Indexing strategy: use per-partition time-sliced inverted index with bloom filters for quick existence checks; sparse index of (time-window -> segment pointer -> summary hashes) to reduce index size on cold tier. Compaction cadence: daily compact for hot tier, weekly for warm, monthly for cold compaction (metadata-only).

Operational controls: feature flag to enable allocator for tenant, emergency global throttle endpoint, backpressure signal integration to front-line routers, and a migration-mode where both old and new controllers accept writes (write-through) during rollout.
rollout_plan:
Week 1-2: unit/e2e tests and integration with RBAC v2 event labels (dev cluster). Week 3: Canary enable in us-west-2 for 5 low-traffic tenants with monitoring dashboards. Week 4: Expand to 20 tenants, exercise quota edge cases and sampling rules. Week 5: Enable warm/cold demotion for canary cluster and validate sparse index query correctness. Week 6-7: Gradual region rollout with performance regression gating. Full rollout contingent on SLOs: <1% increase in 95th pct ingestion latency and cold-read P99 <3s.

Rollback strategy: 1) Flip feature flag to route to legacy allocator; 2) Revert per-tenant retention updates; 3) Rehydrate segments from cold to warm if queries show missing data beyond acceptable thresholds.
progress_updates: 2025-01-23: Spike completed for affinity allocator prototype; basic partition placement logic validated using synthetic load.
2025-01-28: Schema update agreed: add 'rbac_label' and 'allocation_hint' fields to audit envelope. Security OK-ed the schema change for PII considerations.
2025-02-02: Initial cost allocator metrics dashboard in Grafana created (per-tenant ingest bytes, effective sample rate).
2025-02-06: PR #1347 created (ingest-agent envelope) and under review; uncovered edge case for cross-tenant bulk writes in multitenant pipelines.
2025-02-06: Blocker: legacy shard-controller rejects ephemeral assignment TTLs >30s. Coordinating with infra (ENG-21004) to relax check or add compatibility shim.
review_comments: PM (Liam Ortega): Ensure Console shows cost delta estimation before applying a retention change; customers must get an estimated monthly cost impact.
Design (Maya Patel): Sparse index UX must support typical audit queries (actor, action, resource, time-range); will provide query patterns for validation.
Security (Priya Nair): Confirm that SSO/SAML admin events are immutable and cannot be auto-sampled away; propose a preserve-list based on RBAC v2 critical tags.
Infra (Omar Rahman): Cold storage lifecycle needs multipart upload and integrity checks; add an idempotent tombstone marker for moved segments.
